details: The U.S. Federal Reserve increased its benchmark federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a range of 3.75% to 4.00%, the first hike since 2023. This move was widely anticipated by markets and aims to combat persistent inflation. Bitcoin's price saw brief volatility but largely settled, indicating that the hike was already priced in by many crypto investors. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the central bank's priority on price stability.
title: Fed Raises Rates to 3.75%-4.00%; Crypto Steady After Initial Wobble

details: The U.S. Senate voted to block the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act from advancing, failing to reach the 60 votes required. This outcome means that the primary responsibility for regulating the crypto market will continue to fall under the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The failure of the bill led to some negative sentiment and outflows from Bitcoin ETFs.
title: CLARITY Act Fails in Senate, Adding Regulatory Uncertainty for Crypto

details: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) has approved a five-year pilot program for blockchain innovation in stock trading. This initiative allows qualified platforms to trade U.S. stocks using blockchain technology without needing to register as a national securities exchange. This development signals a positive step towards integrating blockchain technology into traditional financial markets.
title: SEC Greenlights 5-Year Blockchain Pilot for Stock Trading
